problem: Deep visual MPC navigation (e.g. Hirose et al.) needs large amounts of online robot experience, and visual servoing has a narrow convergence domain, so visual path following is costly to train and hard to deploy on low-compute robots.
motivation: Visual Teach & Repeat lets a robot follow a sequence of subgoal images without maps or planning. Training an MPC-style policy offline from logged image/velocity data is safer, cheaper and lighter for embedded use. A learned future-image predictor lets the policy be trained with an MPC objective without running the robot.
key_idea: Train VelocityNet offline with an MPC-style loss, using a frozen ViewNet to predict future images from generated velocities, so the robot follows teach-phase subgoal images from a single RGB camera.
insight: Combining an image-reconstruction loss (through the learned view-synthesis model) with a velocity regularizer gives smooth, accurate velocities without online interaction. The reversed forward pass (swapping current and goal images and negating the velocities) acts as data augmentation. The horizon is kept at N=2 to limit ViewNet error accumulation. There are no ablations, so these claims are supported only by design rationale and the error statistics in simulation.
method: ViewNet: encoder-decoder (8 conv layers, 512-d feature concatenated with (v,ω)) that outputs a 2x128x128 flow field to warp the input image into the predicted future image; inspired by Hirose's VUNet.
VelocityNet: 8-layer CNN taking the concatenated current and subgoal images and outputting N-step (v,ω) sequences through tanh, bounded to vmax=0.5 m/s and ωmax=1 rad/s.

Offline MPC training: triplets of consecutive dataset images (I_i, I_i+1, I_i+2) with their recorded velocity commands; two forward passes, the second with reversed roles and negated velocities as augmentation.

Loss: J_j = w1*J_img + w2*J_vel with w1=0.8 and w2=0.3, horizon N=2. J_img is the L1 (MAE) between ViewNet-predicted images and dataset images; J_vel is the squared error between generated and recorded commands, acting as a smoothness regularizer.
Subgoal switching / control loop: send the first velocity for 0.1 s and then pause; advance to the next subgoal when the L1 image difference is at most e_m=17.

Data: 7024 images with velocity commands collected in a ROS Gazebo house with a textured mosaic floor; images resized to 128x128; Adam optimizer, lr 1e-4, trained on T4 GPUs; ViewNet is trained first.

setting.backbone: ViewNet + VelocityNet (custom 8-layer CNNs, trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 7024 image/velocity pairs collected in a single Gazebo house environment
setting.privileged: none at test time (ground-truth x,y and yaw are used only for evaluation)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark and no baseline comparisons; only trajectory-tracking error statistics in one simulated house. The table caption for translation labels the MSE row in meters as printed.
results: In simulation, the robot follows three visual trajectories (pure translation, pure rotation, translation+rotation) with small tracking errors: mean translation error about 0.012 m (MSE) and 0.00504 m for the combined case, and rotation MAE of 1.578°. Rotation is less consistent (std 1.187°), and the combined trajectory drifts near its end. No baselines are compared.
limitations: Evaluated only in one simulated house with three trajectories and no baselines; no real-robot experiments.
Short horizon (N=2) because ViewNet errors accumulate; no obstacle avoidance; results are sensitive to the manually tuned e_m.
Rotation tracking is less consistent, and the combined trajectory drifts near its end.
